title: Every save writes the whole in-memory list, so a second tab silently deletes the other tab's notes
evidence: Driven with two pages in one browser context. Tab 1 loaded [Alpha, Untitled]. Tab 2 created 'FromTab2' and localStorage held [Alpha, Untitled, FromTab2]. Tab 1 then typed one character in its title. localStorage afterwards held [Alpha, Untitledx]. There is no `storage` listener in app.js and no read-modify-write in saveNotes.
failing_case: Open the app in two tabs (a bookmark opened twice, or a restored session). Create a note in tab 2. Edit any note in tab 1. The note from tab 2 is gone from storage, with no message; tab 1 shows 'Saved'.
remediation: Before writing, re-read storage and merge by note id and `updated`, or listen to the `storage` event and reload the in-memory list. At minimum, detect that the stored copy changed since load and refuse to overwrite it.

title: Opening or deleting a note by keyboard destroys the focused button and drops focus to <body>
evidence: renderList rebuilds every button on each call; selectNote (app.js:100) and deleteNote (app.js:121) call it. Driven: focus a note's Open button, press Enter, document.activeElement is BODY. Focus a Delete button, accept the confirm, activeElement is BODY. WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (A).
failing_case: A keyboard or screen-reader user tabs to the third note and presses Enter. The note loads, focus resets to the top of the page, and reaching the title field takes a Tab through search, New note and every Open and Delete pair in the list. After Delete the position in the list is lost the same way.
remediation: After renderList triggered by select or delete, restore focus: to the new current note's Open button after select (or move it to the title field), to the next note's Open button (or the New note button when the list is empty) after delete. Alternatively diff the list instead of replacing the nodes.

quote: try { localStorage.setItem(BACKUP_KEY, raw); } catch (e) { /* storage is already failing; the load message says so */ }
title: Load tells the user unreadable data "was kept" when the backup write can fail silently, and the next save then overwrites it
evidence: backupRaw swallows every error and returns nothing. loadNotes (store.js:47-48, 52-53, 66-67) then returns a message saying the data "was kept under notes-backup" regardless. Driven in Chromium: a 3,000,000-character truncated JSON blob in `notes`, reload. Status showed 'The unreadable data was kept under "notes-backup"', but localStorage.getItem('notes-backup') was null (the second copy exceeds the origin quota). One click on New note then replaced `notes` with a 122-character valid payload.
failing_case: A user with a large (about 3M characters) saved-notes blob that fails JSON.parse (truncated by an earlier quota failure or a crash) reloads. The page says the data was kept. No copy exists. The first New note or edit overwrites the only copy of the original. The user lost data after being told it was safe.
remediation: Make backupRaw return whether setItem succeeded. When it fails, say the data could not be backed up, and do not let saveNotes write over the key until the user has downloaded or acknowledged the raw text (or write to a different key and leave the original in place).

title: A note created or edited while a search is active vanishes from the list but stays open in the editor
evidence: Driven: search 'Alpha' (list shows Alpha), press New note. The editor shows the new 'Untitled' note, the list still shows only Alpha, and no message explains it. The same happens when a title is edited so that it stops matching.
failing_case: Type 'meeting' in the search box, press New note. The new note is selected in the editor but is not in the list and nothing says why; the search box is not cleared.
remediation: Clear the search when a note is created, and keep the current note visible (or show a 'hidden by search' line) while it is open.
